en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines is the highest court and consists of one Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a distinctive crest of brown feathers and primarily hunts flying lemurs in the forest canopy.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, from the balcony of his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago using stone walls.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for rural hospitals.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a two-step forward, one-step backward dance mimicking the river's current.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where each consonant-vowel syllable is represented by a single specific character.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a highly active stratovolcano famous for its nearly perfect natural conical shape.
Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution contains the Bill of Rights, which guarantees citizens freedom of speech and religion.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his masterpiece Spoliarium.
Filipino engineer Gregorio Zara discovered the physical law of electrical kinetic resistance and co-invented the two-way television telephone.
